SUPERVISOR — MIRROR SYMMETRY BREAK, USER report with the perfect test case. Marker: MIRRORSYM-0606 (resolve req_0068).

USER, verbatim: "does this even make sense? why is the two sides of the mesh different if its a mirror image drawing?"
Screenshots — READ BOTH:
  /home/siah/.claude/image-cache/c73c0a8c-84f9-4fad-b702-d4288adbf7bb/34.png — the MESH: left side smooth rounded bumps, right side sharp angular shards, visibly different.
  /home/siah/.claude/image-cache/c73c0a8c-84f9-4fad-b702-d4288adbf7bb/35.png — the CANVAS: a cleanly mirror-symmetric drawing around the center meridian.

A symmetric grid MUST produce a symmetric mesh. Diagnose with their exact drawing, numerically:
(a) sample mirrored cell pairs (u, 1-u) — equal grid values?
(b) mirrored VERTEX displacements on the mesh — equal?
(c) base-mesh test: reset part, redraw the symmetric shape — still asymmetric? (prior grab-sculpts may have left an asymmetric base the depth compounds on)
(d) seam topology: does the u=0/1 wrap meet different vertex density than the u=0.5 mirror line?
(e) display-vs-data: confirm the data is actually asymmetric before assuming (smooth shading can deceive).
Post the numbers, fix at the true layer. P4 pin: symmetric grid in → mirrored vertex pairs equal within epsilon, their trident as the canonical case. READY FOR USER TEST with their own drawing.
